source_text: 24 21.ν Περὶ τοῦ διὰ τὸ ἀπαράλλακτον τῆς φύσεως καὶ τῆς οὐσίας λαλεῖν ἐν πι στοῖς τὴν τριάδα. 21.1 Καὶ τὸ λαλεῖν δὲ ἐξ ἴσου ἐν ἁγίοις τὰς θείας ὑποστάσεις τὴν ἀπαραλλαξίαν τῆς φύσεως καὶ ἐξουσίας ἀπαγγέλλει. 21.2 Ζαχαρίας μὲν γάρ–οὐχ ὁ προφήτης, ἀλλ' ὁ πατὴρ Ἰωάννου–κύριον τὸν θεὸν Ἰσραὴλ διὰ τῶν προφητῶν λελαληκέναι ἔφησεν. 21.3 καὶ Παῦλος δὲ ὁμοίως Ἑβραίοις ἐπέστειλεν· «πολυμερῶς καὶ πολυτρόπως πάλαι ὁ θεὸς λαλήσας τοῖς πατράσιν ἐν τοῖς προφήταις, ἐπ' ἐσχάτων τῶν ἡμερῶν τούτων ἐλάλησεν ἡμῖν ἐν υἱῷ». 21.4 Καὶ Κορινθίοις δὲ περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ ἔγραψεν· «ἐπεὶ δοκιμὴν ζητεῖτε τοῦ ἐν ἐμοὶ λαλοῦντος Χριστοῦ». 21.5 Ὁ δέ γε σωτὴρ παρὰ Ματθαίῳ διδάσκει· «οὐ γὰρ ὑμεῖς ἐστε οἱ λαλοῦντες, ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν ἐστιν τὸ λαλοῦν ἐν ὑμῖν». 22.ν Περὶ τοῦ διὰ τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον, ᾔνουν τὸ ὁμοούσιον τῆς τριάδος, γεγράφθαι, ζῆν ἡμᾶς τῷ πατρὶ καὶ τῷ υἱῷ καὶ τῷ ἁγίῳ πνευματι. 22.1 Τοῦτο ἐπιφανέστατα θεωρεῖν διδάσκει καὶ τὸ γεγράφθαι, ζῆν ἡμᾶς τῷ πατρὶ καὶ τῷ υἱῷ καὶ τῷ ἁγίῳ πνεύματι· ὡς ὅταν Παῦλος διαλέγεται γράμμασι Ῥωμαίοις· «ὑμεῖς λογίζεσθε ἑαυτοὺς νεκροὺς μὲν εἶναι τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, ζῶντας δὲ τῷ θεῷ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν». 22.2 καὶ πάλιν· «ἵνα οἱ ζῶντες μηκέτι ἑαυτοῖς ζῶσιν, ἀλλὰ τῷ ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν ἀποθανόντι καὶ ἐγερθέντι Χριστῷ»· καὶ Γαλάταις· «εἰ ζῶμεν πνεύματι, πνεύματι καὶ στοιχῶμεν». 23.ν Περὶ τοῦ διὰ τὸν λόγον τοῦτον τὸν ἄνωθεν νόμον γεγράφθαι εἶναι τοῦ πα τρος καὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος. 23.1 ∆ι' ὃν ἔφαμεν λόγον καὶ ὁ ἄνωθεν νόμος γέγραπται εἶναι τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος, καθὰ ὁ ἱεροψάλτης λέγει ἐν μὲν λϛʹ ψαλμῷ· «ὁ νόμος τοῦ θεοῦ αὐτοῦ ἐν καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ», ἐν δὲ λθʹ· «τοῦ ποιῆσαι, ὁ θεός, τὸ θέλημά σου ἐβουλήθην καὶ τὸν νόμον σου ἐν μέσῳ τῆς κοιλίας μου». 23.2 Καὶ ὡς Παῦλος γράφει Γαλάταις μέν· «ἀλλήλων τὰ βάρη βαστάζετε καὶ οὕτως ἀναπληρώσατε τὸν νόμον τοῦ Χριστοῦ»· 23.3 καὶ Κορινθίοις ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ ἐπιστολῇ· «ἐγενόμην τοῖς ἀνόμοις ὡς ἄνομος, μὴ ὢν ἄνομος θεοῦ, ἀλλ' ἔννομος Χριστοῦ, ἵνα κερδήσω τοὺς ἀνόμους». 23.4 Ῥωμαίοις δέ· «ὁ γὰρ νόμος τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς ζωῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ἠλευθέρωσέν με ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου τῆς ἁμαρτίας καὶ τοῦ θανάτου». 23.5 Καὶ πάλιν τὴν νέαν καὶ τὴν παλαιὰν διαθήκην αἰνιττόμενός φησιν· «νυνὶ δὲ κατηργήθημεν ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου, ἀποθανόντες ἐν ᾧ κατειχόμεθα, ὥστε δουλεύειν ἡμᾶς ἐν καινότητι πνεύματος καὶ οὐ παλαιότητι γράμμα τος»· καὶ πάλιν· «οἴδαμεν γάρ, ὅτι ὁ νόμος πνευματικός ἐστιν». 24.ν Περὶ τοῦ διὰ τὴν αὐτὴν τῆς ὁμοουσιότητος ἐν τῇ τριάδι αἰτίαν χρηματίζειν ἡμᾶς ἢ ἀνθρώπους θεοῦ ἢ Χριστιανοὺς ἢ πνευματικούς. 24.1 Χρηματίζομεν τοίνυν διὰ τοῦτο ἢ ἄνθρωποι θεοῦ ἢ Χριστιανοὶ ἢ πνευματικοί· δι' ὧν φασιν ἡ μὲν ἐν Σαρέπτοις χήρα πρὸς τὸν Θεσβίτην Ἠλίαν· «τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί, ἄνθρωπε τοῦ θεοῦ;» καὶ πάλιν· «νῦν ἔγνων, ὅτι ἄνθρωπος τοῦ θεοῦ ἅγιος εἶ σύ»· 24.2 ἡ δὲ Σουμανῖτις πρὸς τὸν ἑαυτῆς ἄνδρα περὶ Ἐλισσαιὲ τοῦ προφήτου· «ἰδοὺ δὴ ἄνθρωπος τοῦ θεοῦ μέγας παραγίνεται πρὸς ἡμᾶς». 24.3 αἱ δὲ βασιλικαὶ ἱστορίαι· «καὶ ἄνθρωπος τοῦ θεοῦ ἦλθεν ἐξ Ἰούδα καὶ προεφήτευσεν ἐπὶ τὸ θυσια στήριον τὸ ἐν Βεθήλ»· 24.4 ὁ δὲ ἱεροψάλτης ἐν τῇ ἐπιγραφῇ τοῦ πθʹ ψαλμοῦ· «προσευχὴ Μωυσῆ, ἀνθρώπου τοῦ θεοῦ». 24.5 ὁ δὲ Παῦλος Τιμοθέῳ γράφων τὸ δεύτερον· «ἵνα ἄρτιος ᾖ ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ ἄνθρωπος, πρὸς πᾶν ἔργον ἀγαθὸν ἐξηρτισμένος». 24.6 Αἱ δὲ πράξεις· «ἐγένετο δὲ αὐτοὺς καὶ ἐνιαυτὸν ὅλον συναχθῆναι ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ χρηματί σαι τε πρῶτον ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ τοὺς μαθητὰς Χριστιανούς». 24.7 Ὁ δὲ Παῦλος Κορινθίοις ἐν ἐπιστολῇ διαλεγόμενος· «περὶ δὲ τῶν πνευματικῶν οὐ θέλω ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, ἀδελφοί. οἴδατε, ὅτι, ὅτε ἔθνη ἦτε, πρὸς τὰ εἴδωλα τὰ ἄφωνα ὡς ἂν ἤγεσθε ἀπαγόμενοι. διὸ
pass_a_gloss: [Page number 24 at the head of the copy-text: skipped.] 21.ν [Chapter title:] About the Trinity speaking in the faithful because of the unvarying sameness of the nature and of the essence. 21.1 And the divine hypostases speaking equally in saints also announces the unvarying sameness of the nature and authority. 21.2 For Zechariah, not the prophet but the father of John, said that the Lord the God of Israel has spoken through the prophets. 21.3 And Paul too likewise wrote to the Hebrews: 'in many parts and in many ways God, having spoken of old to the fathers in the prophets, at the last of these days spoke to us in a Son'. 21.4 And to the Corinthians he wrote about the Son: 'since you seek a proof of the Christ speaking in me'. 21.5 And the Savior in Matthew teaches: 'for you are not the ones speaking, but the Spirit of your Father is the one speaking in you'. 22.ν [Chapter title:] About its having been written, on account of the same reason, that is, the sameness of essence of the Trinity, that we live to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit. 22.1 Its having been written that we live to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit also teaches us to see this most manifestly; as when Paul discourses in a letter to the Romans: 'you, reckon yourselves to be dead to sin, but living to God in Christ Jesus our Lord'. 22.2 And again: 'that the living may no longer live to themselves, but to the Christ who died and was raised on their behalf'; and to the Galatians: 'if we live to the Spirit, let us also walk in line by the Spirit'. 23.ν [Chapter title:] About its having been written, on account of this reason, that the law from above is of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. 23.1 For the reason we stated, the law from above too has been written to be of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, as the sacred psalmist says, in the 36th psalm: 'the law of his God is in his heart', and in the 39th: 'to do your will, O God, I willed, and your law in the midst of my belly'. 23.2 And as Paul writes to the Galatians: 'bear the burdens of one another and so fill up the law of Christ'; 23.3 and to the Corinthians in the first letter: 'I became to the lawless as lawless, not being lawless toward God, but within the law of Christ, that I might gain the lawless'. 23.4 And to the Romans: 'for the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus freed me from the law of sin and of death'. 23.5 And again, hinting at the new and the old covenant, he says: 'but now we were released from the law, having died in that in which we were held down, so that we serve in newness of Spirit and not in oldness of letter'; and again: 'for we know that the law is spiritual'. 24.ν [Chapter title:] About our being called, on account of the same cause of the sameness of essence in the Trinity, either men of God or Christians or spiritual. 24.1 So on account of this we are called either men of God or Christians or spiritual; through which [names] they speak: the widow in Sarepta to Elijah the Tishbite: 'what is there to me and to you, man of God?' and again: 'now I have known that you are a holy man of God'; 24.2 and the Shunammite to her own husband about Elisha the prophet: 'look now, a great man of God is coming to us'. 24.3 And the histories of the Kingdoms: 'and a man of God came out of Judah and prophesied upon the altar in Bethel'; 24.4 and the sacred psalmist in the heading of the 89th psalm: 'prayer of Moses, man of God'. 24.5 And Paul, writing to Timothy the second time: 'that the man of God may be fitted, fully equipped for every good work'. 24.6 And the Acts: 'and it came about that they for a whole year were gathered in the church and that the disciples were first called Christians in Antioch'. 24.7 And Paul, discoursing with the Corinthians in a letter: 'now about the spiritual things I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers. You know that, when you were nations, you were led off toward the voiceless idols however you were being led. Therefore [...]'
pass_b_english: That the Trinity speaks in the faithful because its nature and essence admit no variation.

The divine hypostases speak alike in the saints, and this too proclaims that their nature and authority admit no variation. For Zechariah, not the prophet but the father of John, said that the Lord, the God of Israel, had spoken through the prophets (Luke 1:68–70). Paul likewise wrote to the Hebrews: “In many portions and in many ways God spoke of old to the fathers in the prophets; at the end of these days he has spoken to us in a Son” (Hebrews 1:1–2). And to the Corinthians he wrote about the Son: “since you seek proof of the Christ who speaks in me” (2 Corinthians 13:3). And the Savior himself teaches in Matthew: “For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father is the one who speaks in you” (Matthew 10:20).
That for the same reason, namely that the Trinity is of one essence, it is written that we live to the Father, to the Son and to the Holy Spirit.

The fact that Scripture says we live to the Father, to the Son and to the Holy Spirit also teaches us to see this most plainly. So Paul argues in his letter to the Romans: “Count yourselves dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus our Lord” (Romans 6:11). And again: “that those who live may no longer live for themselves, but for Christ, who died and was raised for them” (2 Corinthians 5:15). And to the Galatians: “If we live to the Spirit, let us also walk by the Spirit” (Galatians 5:25).
That for this reason it is written that the law from above belongs to the Father, to the Son and to the Holy Spirit.

For the reason we have given, the law from above is also written to be the law of the Father, of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. So the sacred psalmist says in Psalm 37: “The law of his God is in his heart” (Psalm 37:31); and in Psalm 40: “I have willed to do your will, O God, and your law is in the midst of my inmost parts” (Psalm 40:8). So too Paul writes to the Galatians: “Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ” (Galatians 6:2). And to the Corinthians, in the first letter: “To those without the law I became as one without the law, not being without the law of God but under the law of Christ, that I might win those without the law” (1 Corinthians 9:21). And to the Romans: “For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set me free from the law of sin and of death” (Romans 8:2). And again, hinting at the new covenant and the old, he says: “But now we have been released from the law, having died to that in which we were held, so that we serve in newness of the Spirit and not in oldness of the letter” (Romans 7:6). And again: “For we know that the law is spiritual” (Romans 7:14).
That for the same cause, the one essence of the Trinity, we are called men of God, or Christians, or spiritual.

This, then, is why we are called either men of God, or Christians, or spiritual. We hear these names from the widow in Zarephath, who says to Elijah the Tishbite: “What is there between me and you, man of God?” (1 Kings 17:18), and again: “Now I know that you are a holy man of God” (1 Kings 17:24). The Shunammite says to her husband about the prophet Elisha: “See, a great man of God is coming to us” (2 Kings 4:9). The histories of the Kings say: “And a man of God came out of Judah and prophesied against the altar in Bethel” (1 Kings 13:1–2). The sacred psalmist, in the heading of Psalm 90, says: “A prayer of Moses, the man of God” (Psalm 90). Paul, writing to Timothy for the second time, says: “that the man of God may be complete, fully equipped for every good work” (2 Timothy 3:17). The Acts say: “It came about that for a whole year they were gathered together in the church, and that the disciples were first called Christians in Antioch” (Acts 11:26). And Paul, discoursing with the Corinthians in a letter, says: “Now about spiritual things, brothers, I do not want you to be ignorant. You know that when you were Gentiles you were carried off to the voiceless idols, however you happened to be led. Therefore …” (1 Corinthians 12:1–3).

choices.issue: Old draft a garbled machine draft with wrong psalms and edition numbers
choices.choice: Retranslated the whole section from the Greek. The old English printed the edition numbers '21.' to '24.' and ran each chapter title into the following text; turned 21.ν (the Trinity speaks in the faithful) into 'speaking of the Trinity among the faithful' and 21.1 into 'speaking equally of the divine hypostases'; read λόγον (reason) as 'the Word' in 22.ν and garbled 23.1 into 'Because of whom we said it is the Word'; gave κοιλία as 'womb'. Wrong references: 'Psalm 40' and '(Psalm 40:8; 39:8)' for LXX 36 and 39 (English Psalm 37:31 and 40:8); 'the 89th Psalm (Ps 89 LXX)' for the heading of English Psalm 90; six abbreviated references (1 Cor, Rom, Ps, 2 Tim) written out. 1 Corinthians 12:1-3 now cited at the end of 24.7.

choices.why: Printed page number of the copy-text (page debris); skipped.

choices.term: πι στοῖς, πα τρος, γράμμα τος, θυσια στήριον, χρηματί σαι
choices.why: Words split by line breaks in the copy-text; read whole.

choices.english: the Trinity speaks in the faithful
choices.why: τὴν τριάδα is the subject of the infinitive: the chapter is about the Trinity speaking in believers (21.2-21.5 show the Father, the Son and the Spirit each speaking), not about believers speaking of the Trinity.

choices.term: διὰ τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον, ᾔνουν τὸ ὁμοούσιον
choices.english: for the same reason, namely that the Trinity is of one essence
choices.why: λόγος here is 'reason', glossed by ᾔνουν (= ἤγουν, 'that is') τὸ ὁμοούσιον; the old draft's 'the Word' makes no sense of the sentence.

choices.term: ζῆν ἡμᾶς τῷ πατρὶ … τῷ ἁγίῳ πνεύματι; εἰ ζῶμεν πνεύματι
choices.english: we live to the Father, to the Son and to the Holy Spirit; “If we live to the Spirit”
choices.why: Didymus' argument rests on the same dative with each Person, so Galatians 5:25 is rendered 'live to the Spirit' to keep the parallel; 'live for' is used in 2 Corinthians 5:15 where English needs it.

choices.term: ἐν μὲν λϛʹ ψαλμῷ … ἐν δὲ λθʹ … τοῦ πθʹ ψαλμοῦ
choices.why: Greek Psalm numbers 36, 39, 89 converted to English numbers and checked by verse text. The heading of Psalm 90 is not a numbered verse in English Bibles, so the reference names the psalm only.

choices.english: in the midst of my inmost parts
choices.why: κοιλία is the belly as the seat of the inner self; 'womb' (old draft) is wrong for a male speaker here.
Standard English shape for 'within the law of Christ', set against ἄνομος θεοῦ.
ὧν looks back to the three names; the list that follows (ἡ μέν … ἡ δέ … αἱ δέ … ὁ δέ) is of speakers who use them, so each item is given its own verb of saying.

choices.english: in Zarephath; the histories of the Kings
choices.why: English place-name form; the books of the Kingdoms (1-4 Kingdoms) are the English books of Samuel and Kings.
Didymus reads Romans 7:6 as a veiled reference to the two covenants.

The section ends after the first word of 1 Corinthians 12:3; the quotation continues in the next section, so only the word held here is translated and an ellipsis marks the break. The reference names the full span begun here.
